'''Amber Ellen Boydstun''' is an American [[political scientist]] and [[data scientist]]. She is a professor and director of graduate studies at the [[University of California, Davis]].

== Life ==
Boydstun was born to Faye Ellen Ashley.<ref name=":2" /> Her paternal grandmother Janie Trevarton and her mother Janie Hughes helped maintain a farm and family.<ref name=":2" /> Boydstun's maternal grandmother, Marion Ashley (née DeWolf) was a military wife and homemaker.<ref name=":2" /> She completed a B.A. in philosophy and mathematics from [[St. John's College (Annapolis/Santa Fe)|St. John's College]] in 1999.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Boydstun |first=Amber Ellen |date=2022 |title=Boydstun CV |url=https://ps.ucdavis.edu/sites/g/files/dgvnsk11781/files/inline-files/Boydstun_CV_2022.pdf |access-date=2023-11-18 |website=University of California, Davis}}</ref> Following graduation, she tutored mathematics at the [[Native American Preparatory School]] for a semester.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Yodice |first=James |date=1999-10-18 |title=Old-school education |pages=59 |work=Albuquerque Journal |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/albuquerque-journal-old-school-education/135394263/ |access-date=2023-11-18 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She earned a M.A. (2004) and Ph.D. (2008) in political science from the [[Penn State Graduate School]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> Her dissertation was titled, ''How Policy Issues Become Front-Page News''.<ref name=":2">{{Cite thesis |last=Boydstun |first=Amber Ellen |title=How policy issues become front-page news |date=2008 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=Pennsylvania State University |oclc=435908516}}</ref> [[Frank Baumgartner]] was Boydstun's doctoral advisor.<ref name=":2" />

Boydstun researches the interaction between media and politics.<ref name=":1" /> She joined [[University of California, Davis]] in 2008 as an assistant professor.<ref name=":0" /> She codeveloped a smartphone [[Application software|app]] for students to react to the [[2012 United States presidential debates]] in real time.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chang |first=Richard |date=2012-10-06 |title=College students drum up interest in upcoming vote |pages=B1 |work=The Sacramento Bee |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-sacramento-bee-college-students-drum/135393949/ |access-date=2023-11-18 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Boydstun was promoted to associate professor in 2015 and professor of political science in 2020.<ref name=":0" /> She is the director of [[graduate studies]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Boydstun |first=Amber E. |date=2022-03-11 |title=Amber E. Boydstun {{!}} Department of Political Science |url=https://ps.ucdavis.edu/people/amber-boydstun |access-date=2023-11-18 |website=ps.ucdavis.edu |language=en}}</ref> She is the chief data scientist of the diversity lab.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amber Boydstun |url=https://www.diversitylab.com/team_members/amber-e-boydstun/ |access-date=2023-11-18 |website=Diversity Lab |language=en-US}}</ref>
